case.subject: Product meeting
case.title: Sprint planning: onboarding scope and owners

canvasName: R2-C02 Sprint planning: onboarding scope and owners

segments.text: Let's start the sprint planning meeting. We have a five person product team and two weeks. The goal for this sprint is to ship the new onboarding flow to a small group of beta users, not to finish everything on the backlog. Please keep that goal in mind when we discuss scope. I want us to leave with a committed set of stories, one owner for each, the dependencies, and the risks we accept. First, the business context.
segments.textReply: I’ve captured the sprint constraints and the required planning outputs; the business context is next.WAIT

segments.text: Last month only thirty eight percent of new users completed onboarding. The biggest drop off is at the workspace setup step, where people do not understand whether they need to invite their team right away. Support gets about twenty tickets a week about that screen.
segments.textReply: I’m adding the completion baseline and pinpointing workspace setup as the main friction, backed by support volume.Added the business context: 38% onboarding completion, the workspace setup drop-off tied to unclear invite timing, and about 20 related support tickets per week.

segments.text: The design team has three concepts: a shorter single page flow, a guided checklist that appears after signup, and an import workspace option for users who already have data. We cannot build all three in one sprint. The engineering capacity is sixteen developer days.

segments.text: Story one, shorten the workspace setup page from four steps to two and remove the mandatory invite. That is about three frontend days and one backend day. Story two, add a progress checklist after signup. That is four frontend days, plus analytics, plus two backend days if we want to remember checklist state. Story three, import an existing workspace from a CSV.
segments.textReply: Story estimates are coming in; the CSV import description is cut off, so I’ll capture only the two complete stories.Captured the complete estimates for the setup and checklist stories. CSV import remains pending because its description was cut off.

segments.text: Legal wants an updated consent screen by the end of week one because of a new privacy requirement. That is one day of frontend and half a day of review. And the mobile team needs a small API field for their release, which is half a day on backend. These are not negotiable this sprint, so put them in the capacity budget before we choose stories. The design team recommends story one first.

segments.text: It directly addresses the drop off, it does not depend on the migration, and it is small enough to finish in the first week. Story three is strategically important, but the data model will not be ready until the end of week one, so it is too risky for this sprint.

shapes.title: Sprint planning · post-session summary
shapes.html:
Onboarding sprint · consensus & follow-through

Purpose: Ship a shortened onboarding flow to a small beta group in two weeks—focus on a finishable, measurable slice, not the whole backlog.

Decisions & mechanism

  • Committed: setup reduced from 4 steps to 2, no mandatory invite. Priya leads; Sam reviews frontend; Alex handles backend flag.
  • Measure: Diego captures signup started, workspace created, invite sent; deliver saved SQL view, not a dashboard UI.
  • Invite bug: Alex + Sam fix only if Support reproduces it by Tuesday and it is confirmed by Wednesday; otherwise investigate only—not claimed as shipped.
  • Import: Thursday W1 technical design + migration dependency only; no UI; non-blocking. Diego’s migration is blocked by two legacy tables.
  • Deferred: checklist is not built; keep design ready and place at top of next sprint.
  • Fixed commitments: consent screen by Mei + Priya, legal review Wednesday W1; Alex’s mobile API field targeted Tuesday W2.

Risk posture: Accept checklist delay one sprint; shorter flow may recover activation. Do not ship both flow changes untested. If QA finds a blocker Tuesday W2, delay beta one week.

Support reproduction; fix if confirmedSupport; Alex + SamTue; decision Wed W1
Consent screen + legal reviewMei + Priya; LegalWed W1

Import technical design + migration dependencyTeam / Diego dependencyThu W1

Gates / open risks: No work starts if a dependency is unknown by end of day 2. QA begins only after staging is stable; QA contractor tests Tue–Wed W2. Import migration remains blocked by two legacy tables. Flag any work without an estimate; total engineering capacity is 16 developer days, with fixed commitments reserved first.

Compact timeline: W1 Mon–Wed setup · Tue support reproduction · Wed consent/legal + analytics begins · Thu bug fix, analytics continues + import design. W2 Mon staging stable · Tue API field + QA starts · Wed QA / mid-sprint review · Thu beta rollout · Fri buffer. Monday standup is the next check-in. Post summary in sprint channel today.
